docs.title: Optimization library architecture
docs.text:
Go applications can import pkg/optimization/qubo, pkg/optimization/ising, and pkg/optimization/bruteforce without initializing the compiler. The QUBO package constructs Ising models through the Ising package's public constructor. The exhaustive solver consumes QUBO models. Both model packages reuse internal sparse coefficient, summation, and JSON helpers. The optimization packages use the Go standard library and these mathematical components.

The working example builds a binary objective and an exactly-one penalty, checks a mapped spin assignment, round-trips both models through JSON, and uses exhaustive search.

go run ./examples/optimization/qubo

docs.title: Phase 2D and future language integration
docs.text:
A future compile-time value system could introduce immutable, typed library records for a variable count, offset, and ordered sparse terms. It would need schema-aware signature validation, bounded construction and copying, and typed field access or iteration. An adapter could bind those records to the public Go models and expose pure operations under a future std/optimization module. Phase 2D provides the QAOA Go API and JSON-based CLI. The Smith bindings described here are future work.

The QAOA circuit library consumes the Ising fields and couplings in canonical order together with explicit qubit and parameter mappings. It builds a QAOA cost layer from the existing rotation primitives and reuse the simulator or another backend through typed IR. The mathematical offset would stay in the model for objective evaluation, even when a circuit represents it only up to global phase. An exhaustive solution provides a small classical comparison baseline. The Go package includes the transverse-field mixer, circuit synthesis, and bounded parameter search.

docs.title: Generic constraint penalties in Smith
docs.text:
addExactlyOne(model, [0, 1, 2], 10.0) adds 10 × (x₀ + x₁ + x₂ − 1)². The input list is nonempty, uses valid zero-based indices, and contains no repeats. A zero penalty is allowed and still validates the index list.

addSquaredLinear(model, [0, 1, 2], [1.5, -2.0, 0.5], 1.5, 2.0) adds 2 × (1.5x₀ − 2x₁ + 0.5x₂ − 1.5)². The index and weight arrays must have the same fixed length. Targets and weights may be negative or fractional. Penalties must be finite and nonnegative.

Both calls use the existing QUBO penalty expansion, including its constant term. The constraints example applies both forms through imported helpers. Small penalties can trade constraint violations against other terms in the objective. QAOA sampling can produce assignments that violate a constraint even when the classical minimum satisfies it.

docs.title: QUBO to Ising conversion
docs.text:
Use qubo.Model.ToIsing() to substitute xᵢ = (1 − zᵢ)/2. For QUBO offset c, linear coefficients a, and canonical quadratic coefficients b, the conversion is:

Jᵢⱼ = bᵢⱼ/4
hᵢ = −aᵢ/2 − Σⱼ≠ᵢ b[min(i,j), max(i,j)]/4
offset = c + Σᵢ aᵢ/2 + Σᵢ<ⱼ bᵢⱼ/4

For E = 1 − 2x₀ + 3x₁ + 4x₀x₁, the result is H = 2.5 − 2.5z₁ + z₀z₁. The four assignments 00, 10, 01, and 11 have energies 1, −1, 4, and 6 under both models.

Conversion accumulates contributions as exact rationals before rounding each output coefficient to binary64. This postpones overflow checks until a complete coefficient has been computed. A coefficient outside Float64 range produces an error. Subnormal terms can round to zero, and cancellation among very large rounded coefficients can limit the accuracy of a small energy. The offset remains part of the serialized and evaluated model.

Exhaustive tests compare QUBO and Ising energies to a direct matrix reference using 1e-12 + 1e-12 × max(|actual|, |expected|) on the small test models. Applications with significantly different coefficient scales should choose a tolerance for their numerical conditioning.

docs.title: Building Your First Quantum Optimization Model in Qasmith
docs.text:
Create a file called my-objective.smith and write a two-variable binary objective. No custom Go extension is needed.

import { qubo, addLinear, addQuadratic, addExactlyOne } from "std/optimization/qubo";
import { qaoa } from "std/optimization/qaoa";

fn main() -> MeasuredResult {
    let base = qubo(2, 0.5);
    let linear = addLinear(base, 0, -2.0);
    let interaction = addQuadratic(linear, 0, 1, 0.75);
    let model = addExactlyOne(interaction, [0, 1], 4.0);
    return qaoa(model, [0.4], [0.3]);
}

The unconstrained energy is 0.5 − 2x₀ + 0.75x₀x₁. The penalty adds cost when neither or both variables are selected. Each binding keeps its own immutable model.

qasmith check my-objective.smith
qasmith compile my-objective.smith -o initial.qasm
qasmith run my-objective.smith --shots 1000 --seed 42
qasmith optimize my-objective.smith --max-evals 200 --restarts 3 --shots 1000 --seed 42 --output-qasm optimized.qasm

The simulator returns counts and energy for each observed bitstring. The first bit is variable zero. Expected energy averages across observations. The best observed assignment is a separate result. The optimizer searches for lower expected energy, starts at the source parameters, and leaves the source file unchanged.

To reuse the model, move the declarations that construct it into a public function returning OptimizationProblem. Import that function from the entry program and keep the final qaoa call there. Follow the pure Smith library and package guide to distribute it locally.

docs.title: Add a trusted optimization model builder
docs.text:
The working custom module embeds the public compiler. It creates a one-variable QUBO from a typed input and lets the Smith standard QAOA function build the circuit.

  1. Create an extension.Registry and register plan.OptimizationProblem().Descriptor(). This is the identity the standard QAOA export accepts.
  2. Register a module such as host:custom-optimization with RegisterModule. Export an extension.Function returning the opaque type name. Use exact scalar or fixed-array parameter types, or a numeric array rank constraint.
  3. Implement the Evaluate callback. Inspect dimensions and limits and call ctx.Spend before the work. Construct a QUBO with its public builder, then use plan.FromQUBO and kind.Pack. Optionally supply a typed result decoder.
  4. Set Compiler.Registry to your registry. Call Check, Prepare, or Compile. A compiler uses a registration snapshot and adds its standard modules. Your registration object remains reusable.
import { createProblem } from "host:custom-optimization";
import { qaoa } from "std/optimization/qaoa";

fn main() -> MeasuredResult {
    let problem = createProblem(1.0);
    return qaoa(problem, [0.4], [0.3]);
}

Code can define additional opaque types with extension.NewOpaqueType or NewCheckedOpaqueType. A descriptor's snapshot callback validates and isolates mutable data on pack and unpack. Values from different descriptors with the same name are rejected at the boundary. Registered structured results can apply additional budget checks.

A terminal extension supplies Produce and returns a CircuitPlan with a Build method. It has no access to the compiler's IR storage. The compiler validates measured output, budget limits, and source origins. The ordinary extension.Intrinsic interface remains available for borrowed gates. Type-only CheckTypes may run during check. Value validation, evaluation, and production callbacks run only during lowering.

Host callbacks execute with ordinary Go process privileges. They must be explicitly registered by the embedding application and use their budget context synchronously. Source files can resolve those exports but cannot load native binaries or obtain filesystem, shell, or network APIs through the language.

Use keyed literals for extension.Value, qasmith.Limits, and qaoa.OptimizeOptions. These structs gained fields. Callback signatures for existing intrinsic registrations and the general compiler methods are preserved.

docs.title: Ising Hamiltonians
docs.text:
Qasmith uses z = 1 − 2x everywhere in the optimization libraries. Binary zero maps to spin +1, and binary one maps to spin −1. Variable indices and assignment order are preserved.

H(z) = offset + Σᵢ hᵢ zᵢ + Σᵢ<ⱼ Jᵢⱼ zᵢ zⱼ
zᵢ ∈ {−1, +1}

Use ising.New(variables, offset, fields, couplings) to construct a model directly. Supply canonical coupling endpoints I < J. Field indices and pairs must be unique. Terms may be supplied in any order. The model stores only nonzero coefficients and exposes copies through Fields and Couplings. Use Field(i) and Coupling(i, j) for individual coefficients.

Use ising.Spins(bits) to convert a Boolean assignment and Model.Evaluate(spins) to compute the energy. Evaluation rejects invalid spin values and length mismatches. It uses deterministic compensated Float64 summation and includes the offset.

docs.title: Optimization in Smith
docs.text:
A Smith program can construct an optimization problem with a trusted library and return a measured circuit from a terminal producer. The root tsp.smith uses the four-city TSP example.

import { tsp } from "std/optimization/tsp";
import { qaoa } from "std/optimization/qaoa";

fn main() -> MeasuredResult {
    let distances = [[0, 2, 3], [2, 0, 1], [3, 1, 0]];
    let problem = tsp(distances, 0);
    return qaoa(problem, [0.4], [0.3]);
}

OptimizationProblem is a registered opaque compile-time type. It holds an immutable QUBO-backed model, variable ordering, and optional decoder. Smith can bind it, pass it to a typed parameter, and return it from a pure helper in another module. Its fields are accessible to trusted Go code through the type descriptor's typed API. Smith has no implicit scalar or qubit conversion, indexing, mutation, or array literals of opaque values.

A terminal producer is permitted only as the top-level final returned expression of main() -> MeasuredResult. Classical declarations and pure helpers may precede it. Allocations, borrowed gates, measurements, and calls with other quantum effects cannot be combined with it, including through helpers.

go build ./cmd/qasmith
./qasmith check tsp.smith
./qasmith compile tsp.smith -o circuit.qasm
./qasmith run tsp.smith --shots 1000 --seed 42
./qasmith optimize tsp.smith --max-evals 200 --restarts 3 --shots 1000 --seed 42 --output-qasm optimized.qasm

check validates imports, signatures, static shapes, and effects. It defers host value callbacks and circuit production. Thus a negative distance or invalid start can pass shape checking and then produce a source-aware error during compilation. See the examples.

docs.title: Model composition
docs.text:
scale(model, factor) applies the factor to the constant offset and every term. Zero clears the coefficients and offset while preserving the variable count. Negative factors are valid.

combine(left, right) adds coefficients and offsets by variable index. The two models must have the same variable count and share the caller's indexing convention. No variable remapping is performed.

The composition example combines a two-variable objective with a scaled matrix model. Separate variables hold the unscaled models for reuse.

The generic functions reject any input with an attached domain decoder. For example, a TSP route report describes a particular matrix and constraint encoding, so modifying its QUBO through a generic operation could make the report misleading. Domain-specific transformation policies belong to the library that owns the decoder.

docs.title: Model immutability and resource budgets
docs.text:
Every QUBO transformation returns a validated model snapshot. An earlier binding can be passed to multiple helpers or retained through imports. No fields are exposed for Smith mutation, and opaque values have no scalar conversion.

The generic transforms reject inputs with attached domain decoders. A QUBO value remains generic by construction unless its Go integration attaches a decoder. TSP keeps its established route metadata and continues to work with the QAOA producer.

Model construction charges work before copying terms, allocating matrix conversions, or expanding constraints. Penalties charge their potential pair expansion at positive strength. Repeated transformations therefore share a cumulative work limit even when intermediate bindings are later unused. The model coefficient limit includes the offset. The compiler applies its existing array, variable, depth, step, gate, and layer limits. See execution plan limits for defaults and flags.

Generic intermediate models hold their original QUBO. The final QAOA recipe converts the finished model to Ising. This allows a finite interim QUBO to be scaled before Ising conversion is required. Circuit export and the local simulation width limit remain independent.

docs.title: Pure Smith optimization packages
docs.text:
A Smith helper can both return and receive an OptimizationProblem. Define your model with the standard exports, then expose it from an ordinary public function.

import { qubo, addLinear } from "std/optimization/qubo";

pub fn weightedPair(first: Float, second: Float) -> OptimizationProblem {
    let base = qubo(2, 0.0);
    let a = addLinear(base, 0, first);
    return addLinear(a, 1, second);
}

For a relative module, import it with import { weightedPair } from "./models.smith";. A second helper can accept the result and apply a constraint. The imported example passes a model through two ordinary Smith modules.

To share the function as a local dependency, put the file inside a dependency directory and declare its path in qasmith.json. This manifest format maps a package name to a local directory:

{
  "name": "model-demo",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "myoptimization": {"path": "./packages/myoptimization"}
  }
}

Then use import { buildProblem } from "myoptimization/models";. The working packaged example includes its manifest and package. No registry changes or custom Go host are required. See the general package guide.

docs.title: Optimization execution plans
docs.text:
Compiler.Prepare returns validated IR, the producer's immutable circuit recipe when present, and its source origin. The QAOA recipe in pkg/optimization/plan retains the QUBO-derived problem, parameter lists, layer count, variable order, decoder, and build budgets. Calling Parameters() returns copies. A prepared recipe can build a fresh circuit without simulation or search.

  • compile evaluates the source model, builds the recipe's measured circuit at the source parameters, applies configured passes, and emits OpenQASM with the configured backend.
  • run samples the prepared circuit, evaluates original QUBO energies, and invokes the optional decoder.
  • optimize extracts the recipe and calls the existing generic QAOA optimizer with the source parameters and layer count. It builds a revised circuit and may sample that circuit with a separate deterministic seed. Use --no-sample to skip final measurement execution and --output-qasm to save the optimized circuit. The Smith file is unchanged.

Exact and sampled search objectives are selected with --eval-mode exact or --eval-mode sampled. Both minimize the energy expectation. Results distinguish search expectation, final sample estimate, and best observed assignment. A compiled quantum program without a supported recipe can run but cannot use the general optimization command.

docs.title: Resource limits
docs.text:
Existing array, static step, gate, and qubit limits apply throughout. These additional defaults can be overridden in qasmith.Compiler.Limits or with the corresponding CLI flags.

Resource Default CLI Matrix elements 4,096 --max-matrix-elements Model variables 4,096 --max-model-variables Coefficients including offset 100,000 --max-model-coefficients Charged structured evaluation work 250,000 --max-structured-work Circuit layers 64 --max-circuit-layers

Trusted callbacks charge their work against both structured and static step budgets. The supplied TSP integration checks model sizes before building the QUBO. The compiler revalidates returned IR and prevents passes from changing a terminal recipe's register size or measurement order. The optimizer's limits and the 16-qubit local simulator limit are independent of circuit export.

docs.title: Constraint penalties
docs.text:
Use Builder.AddSquaredPenalty(weights, target, lambda) to add the cost lambda × (Σᵢ wᵢ xᵢ − target)². Supply indexed qubo.Weight entries with finite values and distinct indices. The target must be finite and the strength must be finite and nonnegative.

offset increment = lambda × target²
linear increment at i = lambda × (wᵢ² − 2 × target × wᵢ)
quadratic increment at i,j = 2 × lambda × wᵢ × wⱼ

AddExactlyOne([]int{0,1,2}, strength) uses the same expansion with unit weights and target one. The penalty is zero when exactly one variable is selected and positive for other assignments when strength is positive. To make violations unattractive in a combined model, choose a strength with respect to its other objective terms.

Use Model.Scale(factor) to obtain a new scaled model and Builder.AddModel(model) to combine models of the same variable count. Scaling and composition include their constant offsets. Failed penalty additions and failed model composition leave the builder unchanged.

docs.title: Classical reference solver
docs.text: bruteforce.Solve(model) exhaustively checks assignments up to 20 variables by default. Solver{MaxVariables: n}.Solve(ctx, model) lets the caller lower or raise the limit up to 24 and cancel a running search. Equal Float64 energies retain the lexicographically first assignment with zero before one. Search time is exponential in the number of variables.

docs.title: QAOA circuit conventions
docs.text:
The circuit starts in the uniform state by applying H to every allocated qubit. For depth p, supply exactly p finite gammas and p finite betas. Layer zero executes first. Each layer applies its cost unitary and then its mixer.

The Ising Hamiltonian is H_C = C + Σ hᵢ Zᵢ + Σ Jᵢⱼ Zᵢ Zⱼ. To implement exp(−i γ H_C), each nonzero field emits RZ(2γhᵢ). Each nonzero coupling in canonical order emits CX, RZ(2γJᵢⱼ) on the target, and CX again. The constant offset contributes only global phase. The builder omits that phase from gates and the evaluators include the offset in every energy.

The mixer is exp(−i β Σ Xᵢ), implemented with RX(2β) on every qubit in increasing order. Parameters are numeric radians at circuit generation time.

problem.Build(params, qaoa.BuildOptions{}) returns unmeasured, validated IR. Set Measure: true for terminal measurements. problem.Export(params, options, nil) selects the existing OpenQASM 3 backend. The CLI emits measured circuits and defaults to a sibling .qasm path when -o is omitted.

Variable and qubit IDs match. Basis index bit i is qubit i. Displayed measurement strings start with variable zero, so 100 means x[0]=1, x[1]=0, x[2]=0, or basis index 1. The corresponding spins are [-1,+1,+1].

Circuit defaults match Smith's 4,096-qubit and 100,000-gate budgets. Go build options and the CLI's --max-qubits and --max-gates control these budgets. The local simulator independently supports up to 16 qubits, so larger circuits can be exported within their build limits.

docs.title: QAOA energy evaluation
docs.text:
The objective is the Ising expectation Σ_x P(x) H_C(1−2x). It includes the model offset. qaoa.EvaluateExact uses the simulator's unmeasured statevector and squared amplitude magnitudes. It normalizes small floating-point drift and uses compensated summation. Exact mode is deterministic and uses no measurement randomness.

qaoa.EvaluateSampled builds a circuit with terminal measurements. It computes an estimate by weighting each observed energy by its measured frequency. It returns counts, the estimated expectation, and the lowest-energy observed assignment with its count and frequency. Equal observed energies select the first bitstring lexicographically. Use qaoa.DecodeBitstring to obtain the Boolean assignment.

qaoa.NewLocalEvaluator precomputes one table of basis energies for repeated evaluations. The local evaluator rejects models above 16 qubits before allocating the table. Sampling accepts 1 to 1,000,000 shots per evaluation and is reproducible for a fixed seed. The simulator observes cancellation between gates and in batches of shots. Exact evaluation and table construction check cancellation during traversal.

A sampled expectation carries sampling error. A best observed assignment is one particular outcome, and a classical minimum is available only when the bounded exhaustive solver completes. Float64 rounding applies to all reported energies.

docs.title: QAOA extension interfaces
docs.text:
The QAOA package emits ordinary ir.Program values. Use Problem.Build to feed existing tools, or Problem.Export to select an ir.Backend. Build options accept existing IR passes. The pipeline revalidates the IR, output register layout, measurement order, and gate budget after each pass. The default evaluator uses the unmodified synthesized circuit.

Implement qaoa.Evaluator to supply expectations from another execution method. Implement qaoa.Optimizer to substitute a classical search. The optimizer receives an Objective that returns expected energy. The hybrid helper uses built-in local sampling for its final measurement, even when an alternative evaluator supplies the search objective. Evaluate or build separately to use an external execution pipeline end to end.

qasmith.Statevector and qasmith.SimulateIR expose the existing local simulator for validated IR. Amplitudes and measured-qubit IDs are newly allocated, with amplitudes taken before terminal measurement. Existing source compilation, host intrinsic, backend, and pass interfaces keep their signatures.

docs.title: Proposed Phase 3 architecture
docs.text:
A future library could expose immutable structured optimization inputs, parameter lists, and results through a typed Smith binding layer. That layer should validate the same shapes and limits as Go and keep static circuit construction separate from runtime execution and result handling. A future std/optimization module would depend on that value system. Phase 2D uses Go and QUBO JSON entry points.

For alternative mixers or remote execution, route typed circuits through explicit synthesis and execution boundaries. Keep expectations, sample provenance, and optional classical references distinct in result records. Such integration can reuse the current mathematical models and optimizer interfaces.

docs.title: Hybrid parameter optimization
docs.text:
qaoa.Optimize(ctx, problem, options) minimizes the evaluator's expected energy. The default search polls both signs of each gamma and beta coordinate, starting with a π/4 step. It halves the step after a full sweep without improvement. Additional starts are drawn from a seeded generator, with gammas in [-π, π) and betas in [-π/2, π/2). Starts share the evaluation and iteration budgets and are swept in round-robin order. These intervals initialize restarts and are not hard parameter bounds or assumed periods.

Setting Default CLI Layers 1 --layers Initial gamma and beta per layer 0.4 and 0.3 --gammas, --betas Objective evaluations 200 --max-evals Coordinate sweeps 100 --max-iters Step tolerance 0.0001 --tolerance Seed 0 --seed Additional starts 0 --restarts Objective mode exact --eval-mode exact\|sampled Shots per sampled evaluation and final run 1,000 --shots

Search evaluation and sweep budgets are each capped at 100,000, and additional starts at 64. Convergence means every requested start reached the step tolerance. Reaching a budget returns the best evaluated parameters and reports the stopping reason. The returned counts come from a separate deterministic final seed. During sampled search, using a fixed seed at each evaluation keeps comparisons reproducible.

For Go callers, set Reference: true to enable bounded exhaustive comparison. The CLI enables it by default and accepts --reference=false. The default reference limit is 20 variables and can be lowered or raised up to 24. QUBO inputs use the original model for reference energies. Direct Ising problems use the same exhaustive solver with a spin-mapped binary objective. The optimal sample fraction counts all final assignments whose reference energy equals the reference minimum, including ties. The result explicitly indicates when no reference was calculated.

docs.title: Generic QAOA
docs.text:
Qasmith v0.5.0 builds QAOA circuits from arbitrary supported Ising models or versioned QUBO models. Prepare a Go problem with qaoa.New(isingModel) or qaoa.FromQUBO(quboModel). QUBO conversion happens once and retains the original model for classical comparison.

The CLI reads the existing qasmith.qubo.v1 JSON format. These commands use the three-variable example.

qasmith qaoa compile examples/optimization/qaoa/problem.json --layers 2 --gammas 0.4,0.2 --betas 0.3,0.6 -o circuit.qasm
qasmith qaoa run examples/optimization/qaoa/problem.json --layers 1 --gammas 0.4 --betas 0.3 --shots 1000 --seed 42
qasmith qaoa optimize examples/optimization/qaoa/problem.json --layers 1 --max-evals 200 --restarts 3 --eval-mode exact --seed 42 -o optimized.qasm

QAOA alternates a diagonal cost unitary and a transverse-field mixer. Qasmith minimizes the expected cost, then reports candidates obtained from a separate measurement run. The search is heuristic and has no global optimality or speedup guarantee. Original QAOA paper

See the circuit conventions, evaluation modes, optimizer settings, and Go extension API.

docs.title: QUBO models in Smith
docs.text:
Import std/optimization/qubo to construct immutable OptimizationProblem values. The exports are host-backed adapters to the existing Go QUBO package. The Smith functions and packages that call them need only Smith source.

Every export returns an OptimizationProblem.

Export Parameters Behavior qubo variables: Int, offset: Float Creates an empty model with positive variable count and the supplied offset. fromMatrix matrix: NumericMatrix, offset: Float Imports a fixed-size square matrix as xᵀQx + offset. addLinear model, index: Int, coefficient: Float Adds to one linear coefficient. addQuadratic model, first: Int, second: Int, coefficient: Float Adds to a canonical pair. Equal indices add a linear term. addExactlyOne model, indices: IntArray, penalty: Float Adds the squared penalty for selecting exactly one listed variable. addSquaredLinear model, indices: IntArray, weights: NumericArray, target: Float, penalty: Float Adds a weighted squared equality penalty. scale model, factor: Float Multiplies all coefficients and the offset. combine left, right Adds two models of the same size by variable index, including the offsets.

Here model, left, and right are OptimizationProblem values. Array type names in the table describe trusted signature shapes. Write ordinary fixed-size Smith arrays. Matrices and numeric vectors have homogeneous Int or Float leaves. Index vectors must contain Int values. Integer matrix and weight entries must be exactly representable as binary64. Scalar Float parameters follow the ordinary Smith Int-to-Float promotion rule. Non-finite coefficients and results are rejected.

Indices start at zero. For a general matrix the linear coefficient is the diagonal entry, and a canonical off-diagonal coefficient is the sum of both mirrored entries. Use one triangle for a single contribution. A symmetric matrix with both entries populated contributes their sum. See the Go numerical convention.

check verifies signatures, known array shapes, effects, and evaluable Smith expressions without calling host model builders. Invalid model indices, duplicate constraint variables, incompatible model sizes, and decoder protection are checked during compilation.

docs.title: Quadratic binary objectives
docs.text:
A QUBO is a function on binary variables with zero-based indices.

E(x) = offset + Σᵢ aᵢ xᵢ + Σᵢ<ⱼ bᵢⱼ xᵢ xⱼ
xᵢ ∈ {0, 1}

Use qubo.New(variables) to create a mutable builder. AddLinear, AddQuadratic, SetOffset, and AddOffset return errors for invalid inputs or coefficient overflow. AddQuadratic(i, j, c) accepts either order. Equal indices become a linear term because xᵢ² = xᵢ. Repeated contributions add. Zero-valued terms occupy no sparse storage.

model, err := qubo.FromMatrix([][]float64{
    {-2, 4},
    {0, 3},
}, 1.0)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
energy, err := model.Evaluate([]bool{true, false})

The model in this example evaluates to −1. For a matrix, the convention is E(x) = xᵀQx + offset. The diagonal sets the linear coefficients. An unordered pair contributes Q[i][j] + Q[j][i] exactly once. Either triangle can carry the whole coefficient. A symmetric matrix with equal entries in both triangles contributes twice the individual entry.

Build snapshots the builder. The finalized Model supports value copies and concurrent reads. Term slices returned by LinearTerms and QuadraticTerms are independent copies. Linear and Quadratic return zero for absent terms. Use a positive variable count, including for constant-only models.

Evaluate requires exactly as many Boolean values as the model has variables. Evaluation uses compensated Float64 summation in the order offset, increasing linear index, then lexicographic pair. It reports non-finite intermediate or final energies. For example, overflow can occur in a partial sum even if later terms would mathematically cancel it.

docs.title: Optimization result decoding
docs.text:
Each observation retains its bitstring, count, probability estimate, and original QUBO energy. The first bit is variable zero. The objective estimate weights original QUBO energies by their measured frequencies. An optional decoder gets its own copy of the counts and best-observed assignment and can return a typed domain report through plan.DomainResult. Decoding errors preserve the raw result and report the source of the plan.

The TSP decoder reuses the Phase 3A route report. Valid assignments become closed tours with distances from the original matrix. Invalid assignments retain constraint violations. The CLI prints all raw counts and QUBO energies, then supplements them with feasible and infeasible sample counts, feasibility rate, and best valid route when present. Go callers can inspect each decoded observation by asserting the domain result to tsp.ReportMetrics.

The best observed QUBO assignment, best feasible sampled route, and independent classical optimum are separate. With no valid sampled tour, the CLI reports “none observed” and the Go report has a nil best feasible route. Optimal tour sample rate uses all shots as its denominator and is available when the bounded classical solver completes. The TSP standard decoder enables that solver within its default city limit.

docs.title: Optimization model JSON
docs.text:
Use Go's encoding/json with qubo.Model or ising.Model. Both schemas include a version identifier, positive variable count, constant offset, and dense index-ordered single-variable coefficients. Pair coefficients use sparse canonical entries sorted by (i, j).

{
  "schema": "qasmith.qubo.v1",
  "variables": 2,
  "offset": 1,
  "linear": [-2, 3],
  "quadratic": [{"i": 0, "j": 1, "coefficient": 4}]
}

{
  "schema": "qasmith.ising.v1",
  "variables": 2,
  "offset": 2.5,
  "fields": [0, -2.5],
  "couplings": [{"i": 0, "j": 1, "coefficient": 1}]
}

The encoder preserves sufficient digits to reconstruct finite Float64 coefficients and always orders canonical pairs consistently. The decoder validates the full document before replacing the receiver. It rejects missing, unknown, duplicate, and null members, invalid pair indices or order, repeated pairs, non-finite numbers, and a dense vector whose length differs from the declared variable count. An out-of-order list of individually canonical pairs is accepted and normalized.

A zero coefficient and an absent term represent the same mathematical value. JSON size is linear in the variable count plus the number of interactions due to the dense coefficient vector, even though the in-memory representation is sparse.

docs.title: Trusted optimization modules
docs.text:
Import Export Signature and behavior std/optimization/tsp tsp Takes a square rank-two numeric array and an Int start. Returns an OptimizationProblem with the existing fixed-start QUBO, penalty policy, original directed distances, and route decoder. std/optimization/qaoa qaoa Takes an OptimizationProblem and two rank-one numeric arrays of equal nonzero length. Returns MeasuredResult by terminal production. Array length sets QAOA depth.

The two exports above are trusted Go functions registered in a generic module registry. They can be aliased or imported by ordinary local Smith modules and packages. The travel helper is ordinary Smith code using the host-backed TSP export. Standard module paths are resolved from registrations. Project dependencies cannot claim the reserved std/ namespace.

Numeric arrays are homogeneous fixed-size Smith arrays with Int or Float leaves. The standard adapters convert Int entries to Float64 only when they are exactly representable. They report the relevant matrix or parameter index if conversion would round the value. Float literals already follow Smith's binary64 semantics. Matrix constraints include at least three cities, finite nonnegative entries, and a zero diagonal. The start uses original zero-based indices. See the TSP guide.

The QAOA module depends on the generic optimization problem type. It also accepts a problem from a custom trusted QUBO factory without a decoder.

The QUBO module also builds generic objectives directly from Smith.

docs.title: Proposed Phase 3B Smith integration
docs.text:
Phase 3A exposes TSP through Go and a JSON-based CLI. Smith already supports immutable numeric matrices for distances, integers for the start and layer count, Float arrays for gamma and beta, and fixed-size borrowed registers. These suffice for input representation and parameterized gate helpers.

A reusable library would also need immutable structured types for the validated distance problem, sparse QUBO terms, Ising fields and couplings, and route-encoding metadata. A typed extension API could accept a static matrix and return a compiler-managed value with a declared schema and bounded dimensions. A subsequent extension could consume that value and the two parameter arrays. It would validate both array lengths against the positive layer count and derive the required circuit width from the encoding.

The existing host gate API can apply typed gates to borrowed qubits. A future resource extension could either require the Smith caller to allocate a checked register or expose a compiler-mediated allocator for entry points. An allocator would need to account for qubit and gate budgets, issue stable logical IDs, preserve ownership, and forbid allocation after measurement. Callbacks would emit validated typed operations and retain source origins. No Go callback would obtain raw mutable access to the compiler's circuit or resource state.

Runtime optimization would remain in the execution layer. It would repeatedly build and evaluate circuits with explicit parameter values, budgets, and cancellation, then return counts and route records. Compile-time checking would validate shapes and resource use without executing the search.

A future std/optimization package could expose ordinary reusable functions such as tsp and qaoa through this API. The public Go models, encoder, and decoder would supply the mathematical implementation. Smith support for those imports and structured values is proposed, and Phase 3A adds no optimization-specific syntax or IR.

docs.title: Fixed-start travelling salesman problems
docs.text: The public pkg/optimization/tsp package accepts complete directed or symmetric distance matrices with at least three cities. All entries must be finite and nonnegative, the diagonal must be zero, and the start must be a valid zero-based city index. Triangle inequality is unnecessary. JSON inputs use qasmith.tsp.v1 with start, distances, and an optional name.

docs.title: Encoding and penalty
docs.text:
Call tsp.New(distances, start) or decode a JSON document into tsp.Problem. problem.Encoding() provides Index(city, position) and Variable(index). Variable order is position-major. Within each position, non-start cities appear in ascending original index order. With four cities and start 0, variable indices 0, 1, 2 represent cities 1, 2, 3 at position zero. The next three represent position one.

tsp.ToQUBO(problem, options) adds start-to-first and last-to-start distances as linear terms. Directed transitions from one position to the next appear once as pair interactions. Exactly-one penalties apply to each position and each non-start city through the generic QUBO library. The diagonal is zero, including when two positions select the same city in an invalid assignment.

The automatic penalty is the greater of 1 and twice the upper bound cities × maximum edge distance. The encoder checks that it strictly exceeds that bound and that the penalty offset is representable. Unsafe automatic values produce an error suggesting rescaling or an explicit override. In the mathematical objective, an invalid assignment incurs at least one unit of weighted squared violation and has nonnegative travel cost, so the automatic choice separates it from every feasible tour. Float64 coefficient accumulation and evaluation still have finite precision. Custom positive finite penalties can make the lowest-energy QUBO assignment infeasible.

docs.title: Execution and interpretation
docs.text:
Use tsp.Prepare to create and retain the QUBO, encoding, and a generic QAOA problem. app.QAOA().Build and Export use the standard typed IR and backend. app.Run returns decoded sampled outcomes and can also compute the exact expectation. app.Optimize delegates parameter search to the existing QAOA engine. Its search objective is expected energy including the constraint penalties.

Display strings start at variable zero. problem.DecodeBitstring and Decode validate both one-hot constraints. A feasible assignment returns a closed route and original distance. An infeasible assignment returns its violations and no route. RouteDistance independently validates and evaluates an explicit tour, using the original directed matrix.

Report metrics separate sampled expected QUBO energy, the best observed QUBO assignment, the best feasible route, and the optional independent classical optimum. A sampled bitstring maps to at most one tour. Counts already aggregate repeat observations of that tour. An unobserved valid route is never reported as a sampled candidate. Optimal sample rate uses all shots and requires a completed reference search.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Fixed-start encoding uses (n-1)² variables. The default encoding cap is 4,096 variables, with a separate option for callers who need a different budget. The generic circuit builder applies its own gate and qubit limits. The local simulator supports at most 16 qubits, so four and five cities can be simulated, while six cities require 25 qubits and can still be exported within circuit limits.

The independent tour solver enumerates (n-1)! permutations. It defaults to at most nine cities, with an explicit ceiling of eleven. It reports the number of tied optimum tours and chooses the lexicographically first route. The generic binary exhaustive solver has its separate variable limits. QAOA search is bounded and heuristic.

See the four-city example for all six CLI commands and the Phase 3B proposal for future Smith integration.

docs.title: Building and testing editor tooling
docs.text:
From the repository root:

gofmt -w .
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./cmd/qasmith
go test ./internal/lsp -run '^$' -bench EditorGraph -benchmem

Build and package the extension with Node.js, npm and the pinned official VS Code packaging tool:

cd editors/vscode
npm ci
npm run compile
npm run lint
npm test
npx vsce package --out qasmith-language-0.9.0.vsix

Run real extension-host tests from the repository root. The runner uses an isolated profile and temporary workspace. Set VSCODE_EXECUTABLE to the desktop VS Code executable if using an existing installation. Without that variable the test tooling obtains VS Code.

QASMITH_TEST_CLI="$PWD/qasmith" npm --prefix editors/vscode run test:integration

The VSIX includes the TypeScript extension's compiled JavaScript, its production dependencies and language assets. The Go executable is installed separately. Install the VSIX locally to verify packaging. VS Code packaging documentation

docs.title: Compiler editor analysis API
docs.text:
Clients launching an external server should use LSP. A trusted Go host can embed editor analysis through pkg/qasmith.

var editor qasmith.EditorSession
snapshot, err := editor.Analyze(ctx, entryPath, map[string]string{
    entryPath: buffer,
})

Use absolute paths. EditorPath resolves canonical source identities, including new unsaved files with an existing parent directory. Overlay keys are canonicalized during analysis. Files with no matching overlay are read by the compiler resolver. Errors in the source appear in snapshot.Diagnostics; entry loading and context cancellation can be returned as Go errors.

EditorAnalysis.Documents contains source, compiler tokens, functions, visible binding scopes, resolved occurrences and import exports. SourcePosition uses one-based lines and UTF-8 byte columns. EditorSession serializes analysis calls and holds a bounded parse cache. Treat returned data as snapshots, and identify declarations by symbol ID within the corresponding source version.

The default server uses the bundled standard-library signatures and performs editor-safe static analysis. Editor analysis skips registered type-checking, value and circuit production callbacks. The normal compiler still applies the registered checks.

docs.title: Qasmith language server
docs.text:
Run qasmith lsp --stdio from any editor with an LSP client. The server uses Content-Length framing and reserves stdout for protocol frames. Protocol transport errors go to stderr.

The server maintains versioned in-memory Smith buffers, including imported files. It passes their contents to the compiler editor API. The module resolver, lexer, parser, semantic analyzer and standard-library registry supply the language information. A bounded parse cache is keyed by path and source text. Diagnostics use a debounced analysis worker, and edits invalidate earlier results. Editor analysis skips circuit production and value callbacks. Simulation and parameter search are launched by explicit CLI commands.

Capability Behavior Synchronization Full-text open/change/save/close. Workspace folders and watched-file invalidation. Diagnostics Compiler diagnostic codes and UTF-16 ranges. Source version accompanies open-document results when the client advertises support. Completion Built-ins, visible lexical bindings, types, imported names, module exports and common keywords. Hover Resolved symbol signatures and registry documentation. Definition and references Source declarations and uses across the current graph and graphs of open documents. Registry-provided functions may lack source locations. Signature help Innermost call, with the current argument tracked as the cursor moves. Document symbols Functions and their source ranges from the compiler AST.

An analysis can load up to 128 modules, each up to 1 MiB. The server accepts up to 64 open Smith documents, and JSON-RPC messages are limited to 8 MiB. The compiler's normal static limits still apply. Workspace folders do not add import search paths. Each entry uses the compiler's normal local manifest and path rules. References do not discover unopened, unrelated entry points. Recovery provides analysis for the source prefix up to the first parser or lexer error. A function can report its first semantic error before further errors become visible. The server currently uses UTF-16 full-text synchronization. LSP 3.17 specification

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Highlighting works but live language features are missing. In a trusted workspace, confirm qasmith version returns 0.9.0. GUI-launched applications may see a different PATH from your terminal. Set qasmith.executablePath in User Settings and use Qasmith: Restart Language Server.
  • The executable is inside your project. Automatic discovery skips workspace binaries, including symlink targets within the workspace. An explicitly selected absolute executable in User Settings is allowed in a trusted workspace.
  • The compiler refuses to run in Restricted Mode. Highlighting and snippets remain available. Grant Workspace Trust only for a project you trust. Qasmith does not download packages, load source-specified native plugins or transmit source to a cloud service.
  • A command reports an unsaved file. Choose Save and Continue or save the affected sources and retry. Open Qasmith: Show Compiler Output for errors or process exit codes.
  • Find References omits an entry point. Open that entry as well. References are limited to the current graph and graphs of open documents.
  • The server stopped. Check the Qasmith output channel, optionally enable qasmith.lsp.trace, then restart from the Command Palette.

docs.title: Developing Qasmith Programs in Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
Install VS Code 1.90 or newer and Qasmith CLI 0.9.0 or later. Install the Qasmith extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace or search for "Qasmith" in the VS Code Extensions view.

Set the Qasmith executable path in User Settings (qasmith.executablePath) or ensure qasmith is on your PATH. Open a project directory and grant Workspace Trust to enable compiler processes. Highlighting, bracket matching, comment toggling, indentation, folding and snippets are available in Restricted Mode.

docs.title: Create a QUBO circuit
docs.text:
Save the following as program.smith. The same example is available at matrix.smith.

import { fromMatrix } from "std/optimization/qubo";
import { qaoa } from "std/optimization/qaoa";

fn main() -> MeasuredResult {
    let model = fromMatrix([[-2.0, 4.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, -0.5]], 1.0);
    return qaoa(model, [0.4], [0.3]);
}

Hover over fromMatrix to see its signature and documentation. Use Trigger Parameter Hints inside the qaoa call. For a local imported function, use Go to Definition to open the defining file and Find All References to see references in the loaded graphs. Open Outline to see functions in the current file. Use the fn, main, qreg, for, import and qaoa snippets to start edits.

Try changing model to an undefined name in the return expression. The Problems view shows a compiler diagnostic while the file is still unsaved. Restore the name, then use the Command Palette:

Qasmith command Result Check Current File Runs the compiler's check and reports the result in Qasmith output. Compile Current File Writes program.qasm by default and asks before replacing an existing file. Run Current File Samples the compiled circuit with the configured shots and seed. Optimize Current File Searches for QAOA angles with the configured evaluation budget, then reports results. Show Generated OpenQASM Compiles and opens the actual output beside the source. Restart Language Server Stops the old server and retries startup. Show Compiler Output Opens the Qasmith output channel.

The commands prompt before saving modified Smith or manifest files. Cancel to leave those changes unsaved. The LSP uses the in-memory Smith buffers. CLI commands use saved files.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting under qasmith Default executablePath Empty. Uses PATH. Set an absolute trusted path in User Settings. lsp.enabled true lsp.trace off. Also accepts messages and verbose. diagnostics.enabled true diagnostics.debounceMs 200, with a range of 0–2000. run.shots 1000, with a range of 1–1,000,000. run.seed 42. Accepts safe integers. optimize.maxEvaluations 200, with a range of 1–100,000. optimize.restarts 3, with a range of 0–64. optimize.evaluationMode exact. Also accepts sampled. compile.outputPath Empty. Relative paths resolve beside the source. verbose false. Logs process arguments when enabled.

See Troubleshooting for executable discovery and Workspace Trust.
